# Evaluation (SYNTHETIC scenes; generated by `guetteur eval` and `guetteur bench`)

**Every number below is measured on synthetic OAK-D-style depth scenes with machine-readable ground truth. No physical camera and no AWS were used.**
Thresholds were chosen while developing against this same scene family, so these figures are optimistic for real data (see DESIGN.md 9.3).

Environment: Apple M4 Pro, Darwin 25.6.0, Python 3.12.15, OpenCV 5.0.0 (pin `opencv-python-headless==5.0.0.93`), NumPy 2.5.4, `cv2.getNumThreads()` = 14, `cv2.useOptimized()` = True, frames 320x240 uint16 depth, none (Apple Silicon, CPU only).

3 seeds x 11 scenarios = 33 runs per planner. Event-level scoring of approval *requests* against ground truth.

## Headline

| Planner | scenarios succeeded (all 11 / excl. documented miss) | true alerts | false alerts | misses | precision | recall (excl. documented miss) | median latency |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Guetteur agent (rule planner) | 30/33 / 30/30 | 18 | 0 | 3 | 1.00 | 0.86 (1.00) | 9 frames (1.8 s at 5 fps) |
| naive threshold + executor guardrails | 12/33 / 12/30 | 9 | 9 | 12 | 0.50 | 0.43 (0.50) | 18 frames (3.6 s at 5 fps) |
| naive threshold, no agent, no guardrails | 12/33 / 12/30 | 9 | 27 | 12 | 0.25 | 0.43 (0.50) | 9 frames (1.8 s at 5 fps) |

Receipts: 21/21 honest ledgers fully proven by the vendored prove-it-done verifier (`--min-instruments 2`).
Tamper tests (claim inflated / pointed at wrong pixels or time / re-pointed at another recording; `file:` hash recomputed by the attacker): 24/24 rejected.
Planner calls: 1693 on 4605 frames (0.37 per frame across all scenarios, which include long eventful stretches; the `empty` control triggers 9 calls in 375 frames).

**Tolerance.** A claim passes if the re-measured value is within max(8 mm, 25% of the claimed value) (sensor: 0.08 coverage, drift: 0.01). Inflation beyond that is rejected; smaller inflation passes by design. The tamper test inflates by 2x, plus wrong place/time and wrong input.

**Honest note on the tamper test.** The first run rejected 23/24. The miss was `lens_obstructed` with the *wrong place* tamper: the fault covers the whole frame, so relocating the claimed region leaves the claim true. That tamper is therefore defined as *wrong time* for sensor and drift claims (evidence window moved to the calibration period), and as *wrong pixels* for object claims; the table above is for the corrected definition.

## Per scenario (seed 0 shown; all seeds in `eval/results.json`)

| Scenario | agent | naive + guardrails | naive (raw) | agent alerts (frame, kind) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `empty` | ok | ok | ok | none |
| `shelf_item_removed` | ok | ok | ok | 104:object_removed |
| `shelf_item_added` | ok | ok | ok | 104:object_added |
| `subtle_item_removed` | ok | missed 1, never rechecks | missed 1, never rechecks | 104:object_removed |
| `person_walkthrough` | ok | never pauses | false alerts 3, never pauses | none |
| `person_takes_item` | ok | never pauses | false alerts 3, never pauses | 160:object_removed |
| `noise_burst` | ok | ok | ok | none |
| `slow_drift` | ok | false alerts 3, never compensations | false alerts 3, never compensations | none |
| `lens_obstructed` | ok | missed 1 | missed 1 | 107:sensor_fault |
| `partial_washout` | ok | missed 1 | missed 1 | 134:sensor_degraded |
| `subthreshold_item_removed` | missed 1 (documented) | missed 1 (documented) | missed 1 (documented) | none |

Success means: every expected alert raised in its time window, no other alerts, and the required behaviours present (recheck / pause / drift compensation).
`subthreshold_item_removed` is a **documented failure case**: a 10 mm change is about one filtered sigma and is invisible to every planner. We report it as a miss, not a pass.

## Runtime on this machine (CPU only)

Loop budget at 5 fps is 200 ms/frame. Measured over 1425 frames (2 zones each): median **8.598 ms**, p95 11.644 ms, p99 12.386 ms per frame (perception + planner + executor, both zones). Per zone-frame perception: median 4.671 ms, p95 6.668 ms. Planner call: median 0.009 ms.

| OpenCV 5 call (168x144 zone crop) | median ms | p95 ms |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `inpaint_TELEA_16U` | 1.5002 | 1.6497 |
| `medianBlur_5_16U` | 0.0672 | 0.0759 |
| `morphologyEx_open_3x3` | 0.0073 | 0.0075 |
| `connectedComponentsWithStats` | 0.1499 | 0.2078 |
| `calcOpticalFlowFarneback` | 1.3188 | 1.4329 |
| `resize_INTER_AREA_6x8` | 0.0042 | 0.0043 |

~~None have been measured on Lambda arm64.~~ The table above remains the original local benchmark. Subsequent deployed request samples are in `docs/submission/aws-smoke-summary.json` and the technical report; they are not a rerun of this per-call benchmark.

## Known weaknesses (not hidden)

* Sub-noise changes are invisible (above). Periodic integrated patrol checks would lift the floor; not built.
* Synthetic noise is Gaussian and range-scaled; real stereo has structured errors (edges, reflective and dark surfaces, IR interference). Real clips are the first priority after this prototype.
* Depth cannot say what an object is; claims are about regions becoming nearer or farther.
* Latency is dominated by the persistence rule (10 frames = 2 s); a real deployment would use a longer hold to avoid nuisance alerts.
* The two receipt checks are independent estimators over the same input; they cannot catch a wrong input that was pinned honestly. The digest only proves *which* input was checked.
